description: The line plot titled “Finetuning for different r, WikiHow” illustrates the performance of four different fine-tuning methods on the WikiHow dataset, as measured by ROUGE-1 score across varying values of the rank parameter r (plotted on a logarithmic scale as log r). The x-axis, labeled “log r”, spans from 0 to 9 with major tick marks at integer intervals, representing the base-10 logarithm of the rank r used in low-rank adaptation methods. The y-axis, labeled “ROUGE-1”, ranges from 0 to 35 with major gridlines every 5 units, indicating the ROUGE-1 score, a standard metric for evaluating summarization quality. Four methods are compared: “T5 + LoRA” (red circles, solid line), “MBart + LoRA” (blue circles, solid line), “MBart + AdaLoRA” (orange circles, solid line), and “MBart + LoRA” (green circles, solid line) — note that the green line is labeled identically to the blue line in the legend, which appears to be a labeling error; visually, the green line is distinct and consistently outperforms the others. The green line (“MBart + LoRA”, as labeled) starts at ~23 at log r = 0, rises steeply to ~36 at log r = 4, and plateaus thereafter. The red line (“T5 + LoRA”) begins at ~23, increases to ~28.5 at log r = 3, then slightly declines to ~27 at log r = 9. The orange line (“MBart + AdaLoRA”) starts at ~12, climbs sharply to ~31 at log r = 4, and continues to rise gradually to ~33.5 at log r = 9. The blue line (“MBart + LoRA”) begins at ~12, dips to ~5 at log r = 1, then recovers to ~27 at log r = 9, showing a non-monotonic trend. All lines use circular markers and solid lines, with no error bars or shading.
